prerequisites: Knowledge from high school Mathematics II.
Continuous study habits for the subject.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, make decisions, be creative, reason critically, and communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to make decisions.
Ability to organize and plan.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to work in a team.
Aptitude for motivation for Quality and continuous improvement.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability to adapt to new situations.
Creativity and inventive spirit in solving scientific-technical problems.
Ability for autonomous learning.
Ability to manage information in solving problematic situations.
Ability for critical reasoning.
Ability to fluently use computing at a user level.
Fluently handle the main concepts of Linear Algebra: vector spaces, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization.
Solve systems of linear and non-linear equations using direct and iterative methods.
Apply numerical methods for solving non-linear equations.
Classify conics and quadrics.
Identify different ways to define a curve and calculate its length.
Determine the elements of the Frenet frame and calculate the curvature and torsion of a curve.
Represent curves in the plane and in space.
Identify different ways to define a surface and determine the normal vector and tangent plane to a surface.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK 1.- ALGEBRA. TOPIC 1.- Matrices and Determinants: Definition of matrix. Linear operations with matrices. Matrix product. Transpose matrix. Properties. Types of matrices. Inverse matrix. Uniqueness and properties. Elementary operations. Elementary matrices. Equivalent matrices. Hermite canonical form. Gauss-Jordan method for calculating the inverse of a matrix. Rank of a matrix. Calculation of rank using elementary operations. Definition and properties of the determinant of a square matrix. Application of determinants.
TOPIC 2.- Systems of Linear and Non-Linear Equations: Terminology and notations. Equivalent systems. Gauss elimination method. Rouché-Frobenius theorem. Homogeneous systems: Null space of a matrix.

TOPIC 3.- Vector Space Rn: Definition and properties. Linear dependence and independence. Properties. Basis and dimension of vector space Rn. Coordinates of a vector. Change of basis in Rn. Vector subspaces. Characterization. Equations of a subspace. Basis and dimension of a subspace.
TOPIC 4.- Euclidean Vector Space Rn: Scalar product. Modulus of a vector and angle between vectors. Orthogonal and orthonormal bases. Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization method.

TOPIC 5.- Diagonalization of Matrices: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a square matrix. Properties. Diagonalizable matrix: Diagonalization. Diagonalization of symmetric matrices by orthogonal similarity. Powers of a diagonalizable matrix.
BLOCK 2.- GEOMETRY. TOPIC 6.- Conics: Definition of a conic. Matrix equation. Reduced equation of a conic. Classification and main elements of conics. Study of ordinary conics.
TOPIC 7.- Quadrics: Definition of a quadric. Matrix equation. Reduced equation of a quadric. Classification of quadrics. Study of ordinary quadrics.

TOPIC 8.- Plane Curves: Concept of a plane curve. Expressions of a curve: parametric, explicit, and implicit. Tangent and normal at a point on a curve. Singular points and ordinary points. Plane curves in Polar Coordinates.

TOPIC 9.- Skew Curves: Definition of a curve in space. Equations of a curve. Ordinary point and singular point. Length of an arc of a curve. Frenet frame and Formulas. Tangent, normal, and Binormal line. Curvature and torsion. Osculating, normal, and rectifying planes.
TOPIC 10.- Surfaces: Concept of a surface. Tangent plane and normal line to a surface. Surfaces of revolution and translation. Conical and cylindrical surfaces.
BLOCK 3.- NUMERICAL AND ITERATIVE METHODS. Solving systems of equations.
teaching_methods: Practical classes, seminars and problem solving (Resolution of exercises, problem-based learning, application activities, individual or small group work).
Individual/autonomous study and work (Understanding theoretical content, problem classes, computer practices, bibliographic research).
Tutoring sessions (Guidance on solving exercises and problems).
Theory classes (Expository method, master class, presentation of basic content, solving and proposing exercises and problems).
Computer practicals (Problem solving using symbolic calculation software and result analysis).

assessment_methods.method: Monitoring and control activities for computer practices
Final exam (Block I: Algebra and Block II: Geometry)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on computer practices (20%), a mid-semester algebra progress test (40%), and a final exam (40%). For the progress test and final exam, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 for each block (Algebra/Geometry) is required to pass that block; passed block grades are preserved for the academic year. Students can opt for a global evaluation in the final call (including December call), renouncing previous partial grades, where a single exam covers all content.
